andhraPradesh.headline: Supreme Court asks Andhra Pradesh High Court to monitor Polavaram anti-malaria-drive investigation
facts: On 5 October 2026, the Supreme Court directed the Andhra Pradesh High Court to closely monitor the investigation into a reported incident in Gollaguppa village, Yetapaka mandal, Polavaram district.

The matter followed reports of illness among villagers and the death of a seven-year-old tribal girl after chloroquine was administered during an anti-malaria drive; the alleged causal link remains under investigation.
The Supreme Court bench was led by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and included Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana.
The State informed the Court that an FIR had been registered and the forensic report was awaited.
The order concerns judicial oversight of an ongoing investigation; it is not a finding on the cause of death or liability.
andhraPradesh.summary: The Supreme Court placed the investigation under Andhra Pradesh High Court oversight, asking the High Court to monitor it closely. The direction is significant for public-health programme accountability in a tribal area, while the cause of the reported illness and death remains to be established.
andhraPradesh.staticLink: Article 21; access to healthcare; judicial review and accountability in public administration.
andhraPradesh.prelimsTakeaway: Distinguish judicial monitoring of an investigation from a final judgment on causation or liability; the incident is from Gollaguppa in Polavaram district.
andhraPradesh.mainsAngle: Examine safeguards for informed, safe implementation of public-health interventions in tribal areas and the role of judicial oversight when serious adverse outcomes are reported.
andhraPradesh.apLink: The investigation concerns a reported anti-malaria-drive incident in Gollaguppa village, Yetapaka mandal, Polavaram district, Andhra Pradesh.

andhraPradesh.headline: Andhra Pradesh sets a target of five lakh women entrepreneurs under Swayam AP
facts: At a review meeting on 5 October, the Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister set a target of creating five lakh women entrepreneurs and asked the Society for Elimination of Rural Poverty (SERP) and Mission for Elimination of Poverty in Municipal Areas (MEPMA) to support the effort.

Officials were directed to develop Swayam AP as a common brand for products made by DWCRA women, with standardised quality, modern packaging, e-commerce, signature stores and an integrated marketing network.
Officials reported that ₹68,585 crore in loans had been mobilised to support women; this was reported as mobilised support, not a newly announced grant.
Officials said Stree Nidhi had provided ₹4,800 crore in loans to 4.73 lakh women and that SHG members were producing more than 23,000 products.
The initiative includes training, market access, mentoring and incubation, with participation from more than 60 organisations reported.
andhraPradesh.summary: The State’s 5 October review connected its five-lakh women-entrepreneur target with a common brand and stronger market access for DWCRA products. Swayam AP is intended to link SHG production with quality standards, digital sales and retail channels; the loan figures were reported as existing support, not a new allocation.
andhraPradesh.staticLink: Women’s self-help groups; livelihood promotion; financial inclusion; inclusive and rural development.
andhraPradesh.prelimsTakeaway: SERP serves rural-poverty programmes and MEPMA serves urban-poverty programmes; Swayam AP is the proposed common brand for DWCRA products.
andhraPradesh.mainsAngle: Assess how branding, quality assurance, credit, skills and market linkages can help SHGs move from subsistence livelihoods to sustainable women-led enterprises.
andhraPradesh.apLink: The target and Swayam AP directions apply to Andhra Pradesh’s DWCRA and self-help-group network statewide.

andhraPradesh.headline: Andhra Pradesh inaugurates six urban forests and expands eco-tourism initiatives
facts: On 6 October, Andhra Pradesh inaugurated six new urban forests under the Nagar Van Yojana, taking the reported State total from 19 to 25.
The six forests cover about 305 hectares and were developed at a reported cost of ₹13 crore.
The event also highlighted eco-tourism initiatives including the Nallamala Jungle Safari at Velugodu and a canopy walk and trekking route at Maredumilli.
The initiatives combine urban green space and nature-awareness facilities with the stated aim of supporting local and tribal livelihoods through eco-tourism.
AP Forest Development Corporation officials received a PRAMAAN certificate at the event; PIB had reported the corporation’s certificate for plantations covering 33,000 hectares on 29 September 2026.
andhraPradesh.summary: The 6 October inaugurations expanded the State’s reported urban-forest network to 25 and included eco-tourism facilities associated with Nallamala and Maredumilli. The developments connect urban greening and nature-based tourism with local livelihood objectives; the PRAMAAN certificate itself had already been awarded to APFDC on 29 September.
andhraPradesh.staticLink: Urban forestry; biodiversity conservation; sustainable tourism; community-based livelihoods.
andhraPradesh.prelimsTakeaway: Nagar Van Yojana supports urban green spaces; PRAMAAN is the Indian Forest and Wood Certification Scheme’s certification framework.
andhraPradesh.mainsAngle: Discuss how urban forests and community-linked eco-tourism can contribute to public well-being, conservation and tribal livelihoods, while requiring safeguards against ecological overuse.
andhraPradesh.apLink: All six urban forests and the cited eco-tourism initiatives are in Andhra Pradesh; the certificate recipient is the Andhra Pradesh Forest Development Corporation.

national.headline: Union Cabinet approves ₹10,000-crore commitment for SME Growth Fund
facts: The Union Cabinet approved a Government of India commitment of ₹10,000 crore for establishing the SME Growth Fund.
The fund is designed to provide patient growth-equity capital to viable, scalable small and medium enterprises.
It will be structured as an Alternative Investment Fund and is intended to support manufacturing, services, technology, innovation and strategic value chains.
The initiative was provided for in Union Budget 2026–27; the Cabinet approval is not evidence that investments have already been disbursed.
national.summary: The Cabinet approved a ₹10,000-crore commitment to establish the SME Growth Fund, targeting the growth-equity gap faced by SMEs seeking to scale. The fund is approved for establishment; the announcement does not mean the full amount has been invested in businesses.
national.staticLink: MSME development, alternative investment funds and access to growth capital
national.prelimsTakeaway: Remember the ₹10,000-crore commitment, AIF structure and growth-equity focus of the SME Growth Fund.
national.mainsAngle: Assess how patient equity capital can help SMEs scale, adopt technology and strengthen manufacturing and exports, while considering fund governance and selection transparency.

- **When:** **6 October 2026**

# 2. Structure and purpose
- **Structure:** **Alternative Investment Fund (AIF)**
- **Objective:** Patient growth-equity capital for viable, scalable small and medium enterprises
- **Focus areas:**
| Area | Focus |
|---|---|
| **Manufacturing** | **SME growth** |

| **Technology** | **SME growth** |

national.headline: Cabinet approves Integrated Transport & Logistics Authority
facts: The Union Cabinet approved an SPV named the Integrated Transport & Logistics Authority (ITLA).
ITLA is intended to coordinate integrated transport and logistics planning, research, project appraisal, monitoring and impact assessment.
It is to prepare a National Transport Master Plan with a planning horizon of at least ten years, covering multiple transport modes.
ITLA is to technically appraise and monitor central infrastructure projects costing ₹500 crore or more; financial appraisal remains with existing mechanisms.
Its proposed National Transport Data Repository will integrate transport and logistics datasets for planning and analysis.
national.summary: The Cabinet approved ITLA as a coordinating institution intended to address fragmented planning across transport ministries and agencies. Its remit includes a long-term multimodal master plan and technical appraisal and monitoring of central projects costing at least ₹500 crore.
national.staticLink: Multimodal transport, logistics policy and institutional coordination in infrastructure planning
national.prelimsTakeaway: ITLA is an approved SPV; note its 10-year-plus National Transport Master Plan and ₹500-crore technical-appraisal threshold.
national.mainsAngle: Examine whether a unified planning and data institution can improve multimodal connectivity, project coordination and logistics efficiency, and identify safeguards needed to avoid overlapping mandates.

|---|---|
| **Integrated planning** | Coordinate transport and logistics planning across modes |

national.headline: Rural Development Ministry notifies 375 permissible works under VB–G RAM G
facts: The Ministry of Rural Development notified a schedule of 375 permissible works under the Viksit Bharat – Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin) Act, 2025.
The schedule expands the permissible-work list by 41% from the previous framework’s 266 works.
The four pillars are Water Security (128 works), Core Rural Infrastructure (111), Livelihood-related Infrastructure (98) and Disaster Preparedness (38).
Works are to originate through decentralised Viksit Gram Panchayat Plans approved by the Gram Sabha.
The notification expands the work schedule; it does not by itself establish that all listed works have been completed or funded.
national.summary: The Ministry notified 375 permissible works under the VB–G RAM G framework, organised around water security, rural infrastructure, livelihoods and disaster preparedness. The schedule is 41% broader than the previous list and links employment works to Gram Sabha-approved local plans.
national.staticLink: Rural employment, decentralised planning, Gram Sabha and creation of durable rural assets
national.prelimsTakeaway: Recall the four work pillars and the 375-work total, including 128 water-security works.
national.mainsAngle: Discuss how linking rural wage employment with water security, resilient infrastructure and local planning may improve asset quality and climate resilience, while requiring transparent selection and social audits.

national.headline: HSL launches first indigenous Fleet Support Ship ‘Surya’ at Visakhapatnam
facts: At Hindustan Shipyard Limited (HSL), Visakhapatnam, the Defence Minister launched Fleet Support Ship FSS-1, named ‘Surya’, and laid the keel of FSS-5.
The event also inaugurated upgraded Slipway-4 and a 300-tonne Goliath Crane at HSL.

The indigenously designed and built ships are intended to support naval operations through at-sea replenishment; planned features include cargo and fluid capacity, maintenance workshops, a helicopter deck and self-defence systems.
The upgraded slipway is designed to support construction and launch of ships up to 45,000 deadweight tonnes.
This is a launch milestone for FSS-1, not completion or operational induction of the ship.
national.summary: Previous: HSL’s Fleet Support Ship programme and earlier milestones had been covered. Today: FSS-1 ‘Surya’ was launched, the keel of FSS-5 was laid, and upgraded shipyard infrastructure was inaugurated at Visakhapatnam.
national.staticLink: Andhra Pradesh’s maritime geography, defence industrialisation and indigenous shipbuilding
national.prelimsTakeaway: FSS-1 ‘Surya’ was launched at HSL, Visakhapatnam; keel laying is a construction milestone, not completion.
national.mainsAngle: Evaluate how naval shipbuilding at HSL can build maritime logistics capability and deepen Andhra Pradesh’s industrial ecosystem, while requiring skilled labour, supply-chain development and timely delivery.
national.apLink: HSL is in Visakhapatnam, Andhra Pradesh; the launch, keel-laying and infrastructure inauguration took place at the state’s shipyard.

national.headline: Defence Ministry signs ₹661.50-crore BrahMos fire-control and launcher contract for Navy
facts: The Ministry of Defence signed a ₹661.50-crore contract with BrahMos Aerospace Private Limited for fire-control systems and launchers for Indian Navy ships.
The procurement is under the Buy (Indian-IDDM) category.
The project has a minimum 68% indigenous-content requirement and is expected to generate employment over three years.
BrahMos is the Navy’s primary ship-borne surface-to-surface missile system for maritime strike operations.
The contract covers fire-control systems and launchers; it is not a claim that new missiles or ships have already entered service.
national.summary: The Ministry of Defence signed a ₹661.50-crore contract for BrahMos fire-control systems and launchers for Indian Navy ships. The procurement’s Buy (Indian-IDDM) category and minimum 68% indigenous content connect the contract to domestic defence manufacturing.
national.staticLink: Defence procurement categories, indigenisation and maritime security
national.prelimsTakeaway: Note the contract value, Buy (Indian-IDDM) category and minimum 68% indigenous content.
national.mainsAngle: Discuss how domestic defence procurement can build industrial capability and supply-chain participation while strengthening naval readiness and maritime security.

national.headline: India’s steel output and consumption rise in the first half of FY 2026–27
facts: The Ministry of Steel released provisional sector data for September and April–September 2026, based on Joint Plant Committee data.
April–September crude-steel production was 85.1 million tonnes, up 2.9% year-on-year from 82.7 million tonnes.
Finished-steel production was 81.8 million tonnes, up 3.7% from 78.8 million tonnes.
Finished-steel consumption was 84.9 million tonnes, up 7.5% from 79.0 million tonnes.
The Ministry reported that 101 steel producers had received green-steel certificates by September 2026.
national.summary: The Ministry of Steel reported year-on-year growth in crude-steel production, finished-steel production and consumption in April–September 2026. The figures are provisional and provide a snapshot of industrial activity for the first half of FY 2026–27.
national.staticLink: Industrial growth, steel-sector indicators and green steel
national.prelimsTakeaway: For April–September 2026, crude-steel production was 85.1 Mt (+2.9%) and finished-steel consumption was 84.9 Mt (+7.5%) year-on-year.
national.mainsAngle: Relate rising steel output and demand to infrastructure and manufacturing growth, while considering emissions intensity, recycling and the transition to low-carbon steel.

national.headline: MoSPI proposes broader coverage for the Index of Services Production
facts: MoSPI published an approach paper proposing how to expand the monthly Index of Services Production (ISP).
The trial ISP, with 2024–25 as its base year, began compiling monthly data for the formal sector in July 2026.
The initial framework covered 19 service sub-sectors, representing about 60% of services-sector GVA.
The proposed additions are Education, Human Health and Residential Care, and Public Administration and Defence.
MoSPI estimated that adding these areas could raise coverage to about 78.4% of services-sector GVA; feedback was invited by 16 October 2026.
national.summary: MoSPI published a proposal to broaden the ISP by adding three currently excluded service areas. The change is proposed, not yet a finalised expansion; the Ministry invited stakeholder feedback on its methodology.
national.staticLink: National income accounting, services-sector measurement and official statistics
national.prelimsTakeaway: The proposed additions could take ISP coverage from about 60% to 78.4% of services-sector GVA; the 2024–25 base-year trial began in July 2026.
national.mainsAngle: Explain why comprehensive, timely services data matters for economic policy, and assess the methodological challenge of measuring non-market and public services.

national.headline: ARIES-coordinated study reports decade-long observations of blazar OJ 287
facts: The Department of Science and Technology publicised a multi-institution study coordinated by Aryabhatta Research Institute of Observational Sciences (ARIES), Nainital.
The research team analysed observations of blazar OJ 287 gathered from 2015 to 2025 using two dozen telescopes.
OJ 287 is studied as a candidate binary supermassive-black-hole system with an approximately 12-year orbital cycle.
The research paper reports a central black-hole mass estimate of at least 3.89 billion solar masses based on optical spectra from low-flux states.
The study connects long-term optical observations with multimessenger astronomy, which combines observations across different signal types and electromagnetic bands.
national.summary: DST highlighted an ARIES-coordinated international study using a decade of observations to examine the variable blazar OJ 287. The findings add observational data relevant to studying black-hole systems, relativistic jets and multimessenger astronomy.
national.staticLink: Blazars, supermassive black holes and multimessenger astronomy
national.prelimsTakeaway: ARIES is an autonomous DST institute; OJ 287 is a blazar studied as a binary supermassive-black-hole candidate.
national.mainsAngle: Use this research to illustrate the role of long-term, international and multi-wavelength collaboration in frontier astronomy and the development of India’s research capacity.

sources.title: A decade of cosmic flickering reveals new clues about a rare giant binary black hole system
sources.publisher: Press Information Bureau, Department of Science and Technology

- **Central black-hole mass estimate:** At least **3.89 billion solar masses**, based on optical spectra from low-flux states
- **Research team:** Multi-institution team; study coordinated by **ARIES**

# 3. Significance
- **Multimessenger astronomy:** Combines observations across different signal types and electromagnetic bands
- **Research connection:** Long-term optical observations relevant to black-hole systems, relativistic jets and multimessenger astronomy
- ⚠ **Trap:** **OJ 287** is studied as a binary supermassive-black-hole candidate; the item does not state that the system is conclusively established
> Exam angle: Identify **ARIES, Nainital**, **OJ 287** and the decade-long **2015–2025** observations.

national.headline: National conclave begins deliberations on constitutional rights of tribal communities
facts: The Ministry of Tribal Affairs inaugurated a two-day National Conclave on Constitutional Rights and Legal Provisions for Tribal Communities in New Delhi on 6 October.
The conclave brings together tribal-welfare and revenue officials from states and Union Territories, along with experts.
More than 75 delegates from around 30 states and Union Territories were reported to be attending.
Discussions were intended to address barriers to accessing constitutional rights and safeguards, including documentation, digitisation, grievance redressal and inter-State verification.
The ministry said the deliberations were expected to inform recommendations and practical measures; no final recommendations were reported in the inauguration release.
national.summary: A two-day national conclave opened in New Delhi to discuss implementation challenges around constitutional rights and legal safeguards for tribal communities. The opening-day release described the agenda and attendance; it did not report final policy decisions.

international.headline: 2026 Nobel Prize in Physics awarded to Francis Halzen for IceCube neutrino research
facts: The Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences awarded the 2026 Nobel Prize in Physics to Francis Halzen of the University of Wisconsin–Madison.
The award recognised his decisive contributions to the IceCube Neutrino Observatory and the discovery of high-energy neutrinos of astrophysical origin.
IceCube uses light sensors embedded in Antarctic ice to detect neutrinos and investigate distant, high-energy cosmic processes.
No direct AP-specific link established.
international.summary: Francis Halzen received the 2026 Nobel Prize in Physics for work that helped establish the IceCube Neutrino Observatory and advance the detection of astrophysical neutrinos. The research illustrates how large international scientific collaborations and specialised observatories can open new ways to study the universe.

international.prelimsTakeaway: IceCube is a neutrino observatory embedded in Antarctic ice; the 2026 Physics Nobel recognised Francis Halzen’s contributions to it and to astrophysical neutrino discovery.
international.mainsAngle: Use the award to discuss how international research infrastructure, long-term public investment and cross-border collaboration advance frontier science.

international.headline: First Global Heat Forum opens in Bangkok to mobilise action and investment on extreme heat
facts: The first Global Heat Forum opened in Bangkok, Thailand, on 6 October and is scheduled for 6–9 October 2026.
The forum brought together nearly 600 scientists, business leaders, philanthropists and health experts to advance responses to extreme heat.
Organisers include the World Meteorological Organization, the Global Heat Health Information Network and the Asian Development Bank, alongside partner organisations.
The forum focuses on heat governance, health protection and mobilising finance for resilience.

international.headline: Kenya confirms its first imported Bundibugyo virus disease case; WHO supports response
facts: Kenya confirmed its first laboratory-confirmed imported case of Bundibugyo virus disease (BVD) on 6 October 2026.
The patient had travelled from the Democratic Republic of the Congo through Uganda to Nairobi, where the patient was isolated; the patient died on 5 October.
Kenya notified WHO under the International Health Regulations (2005) and began case investigation, contact monitoring and enhanced surveillance.
WHO reported that Kenya had screened more than 652,000 incoming travellers and trained about 5,000 health workers in Ebola prevention and management as of 6 October.
No direct AP-specific link established.
international.summary: Kenyan authorities confirmed an imported case of Bundibugyo virus disease in a traveller who had recently been in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Uganda. WHO said response measures included surveillance, contact follow-up and screening at high-risk points of entry; this was a cross-border public-health event rather than evidence of wider transmission in Kenya.
international.staticLink: International Health Regulations, epidemic preparedness and cross-border disease surveillance
international.prelimsTakeaway: Bundibugyo virus is one of the viruses that causes Ebola disease; Kenya reported its first imported BVD case on 6 October 2026.
international.mainsAngle: Assess how the International Health Regulations, laboratory confirmation, points-of-entry screening and coordinated regional response support outbreak containment.

international.headline: UN Secretary-General visits Pakistan and urges diplomacy to end US–Iran conflict
facts: UN Secretary-General António Guterres began an official visit to Pakistan on 6 October 2026.
In Islamabad, he called for an end to the US–Iran conflict and highlighted its effects on global trade.
The UN said Guterres acknowledged Pakistan’s diplomatic role in efforts connected with the June 17 Islamabad memorandum, a subsequent ceasefire and a framework for further negotiations.
During the visit, he met Pakistani officials and visited the United Nations Military Observer Group in India and Pakistan (UNMOGIP).
No direct AP-specific link established.
international.summary: During his Pakistan visit, Guterres called for an end to the US–Iran conflict, a return to diplomacy and restoration of navigational rights and freedoms under international law. The visit also brought attention to Pakistan’s role in regional diplomacy and to UNMOGIP, the UN observer mission associated with India–Pakistan relations.
international.staticLink: United Nations, conflict resolution, international law and India–Pakistan relations
international.prelimsTakeaway: UNMOGIP stands for the United Nations Military Observer Group in India and Pakistan; Guterres visited its headquarters during his Pakistan visit.
international.mainsAngle: Examine the role of the UN Secretary-General and regional diplomacy in conflict de-escalation, protection of maritime navigation and reduction of disruption to global trade.

mcqs.question: Which of the following correctly describes the Union Cabinet-approved SME Growth Fund?
options: A. A ₹10,000-crore commitment intended to provide patient growth-equity capital to viable, scalable SMEs
B. A ₹10,000-crore grant already disbursed to all registered SMEs
C. A fund restricted to public-sector steel producers
D. A fund administered as a transport infrastructure project
mcqs.explanation: The Cabinet approved a ₹10,000-crore Government of India commitment for an Alternative Investment Fund intended to support viable, scalable SMEs. Approval does not establish that investments have been disbursed.
